answer: Interleaved Arrival Windows. Agents must submit work requests in staggered 10-minute windows, and each identity's first three windows are recorded as its unique rhythm signature. A clone farm forced to mimic varied rhythms hits a summit of scheduling overhead, since faking distinct onset patterns across hundreds of agents costs more coordination traffic than the farm earns. Historic baseline traffic from the tundra deployment sets the tolerance band. Any identity whose window timing clusters with others gets throttled to sable-tier queue priority, paying latency penalties per task.
